title: Emergency transponder squawk codes
text: Transponder emergency codes: squawk 7500 indicates unlawful interference (hijacking); squawk 7600 indicates a radio communication failure (lost communications); squawk 7700 indicates a general emergency. Air traffic controllers treat any of these codes as an immediate priority emergency.

title: Illustrative incident report: engine failure during climb
text: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE - not a real NTSB report. During the initial climb the flight crew reported a loss of thrust from the right engine, declared an emergency and squawked 7700, dumped fuel, and returned to the departure airport for an overweight landing with no injuries.

title: Illustrative incident report: loss of separation
text: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE - not a real NTSB report. Two aircraft on crossing tracks experienced a loss of separation after a level-off clearance was read back incorrectly; TCAS resolution advisories were followed and separation was restored without further event.
